original_text:
With this resume, I got selected by 7+ companies for Data Engineering roles 
(Impetus, Deloitte, Coforge, Brillio, LTC etc…)

If you're struggling to get interview calls despite strong skills, the problem might be your resume. Here’s how I optimised mine to stand out:

✔️ Tailor your resume for each role
Don’t send the same version everywhere. Highlight tools and tech stacks mentioned in the JD. If it says "Airflow" or "Azure," make sure those aren’t hidden in a corner.

✔️ Add impact, not just activities
Instead of: “Built data pipelines using Spark”
Say: “Built scalable Spark pipelines that reduced processing time by 40%” Companies want outcomes, not just actions.

✔️ Keep it clean and keyword-optimised
Your resume should pass through ATS bots and impress hiring managers. Include keywords like PySpark, Azure, Airflow, Snowflake, etc., where relevant.

✔️ Highlight projects and certifications
Personal/side projects and certifications (like Azure DP-203, Snowflake COF-C02) show your commitment to growth — they set you apart from others.

✔️ Keep it short but deep
Focus on the depth of your experience with tools like Spark, Hive, Kafka, and Python — not on everything you’ve ever done.

📌 If you’re applying for data engineering roles in 2025, take time to audit your resume.
 It’s your first impression, make it count.

Note → Even the best resume won’t matter if your skills don’t back it up. You need deep knowledge of tools like Spark, SQL, Python, Airflow, and real-world data systems.
